title: Printing and integrating a twin-pusher fixed-wing aircraft
intro: Tornado V2 airframe fabrication, Pixhawk 6C integration and the checks behind field testing.
sections: Start with the airframe and its interfaces

For these builds I used the Titan Dynamics Tornado V2 airframe design. My work covered printing and assembly, propulsion and avionics integration, configuration and testing. The two pusher motors and conventional tail distinguish this aircraft from the four-lift-motor QuadPlanes elsewhere in the portfolio.
Balance printing weight with build practicality

I printed the shown airframe builds in ABS using 3% infill and one perimeter, balancing airframe weight with practical rigidity for assembly and handling. The photographs follow the work from wing and fuselage sections on the printer to laid-out parts and assembled aircraft.
Connect propulsion, surfaces and avionics

The build paired Pixhawk 6C with ArduPlane 4.6.3 and twin-pusher propulsion. I integrated navigation, power and onboard wiring, and worked through control-surface directions, stabilization response and differential-thrust checks. Configuration and log review helped connect each test to the next integration step.
Keep the public evidence useful

The open-fuselage views show the hardware integration, while the assembled aircraft images show the finished build stages. The log-review visual has its satellite map and identifying information removed. It provides illustrative review context, not exact flight-path or performance data.

title: Building a 2.2 m QuadPlane as one connected system
intro: Lift propulsion, cruise propulsion and avionics had to work together before field testing.
sections: The challenge: two flight regimes, one aircraft

The Cube Orange QuadPlane combined four lift motors with separate forward propulsion. That made the integration broader than mounting a flight controller. Airframe assembly, power distribution, control electronics and radio links all had to fit into one testable aircraft.
Working through the integration sequence

I integrated the structural components, propulsion, autopilot electronics, GNSS, RC and telemetry, then worked through sensor calibration and configuration. ArduPilot and PX4 workflows formed part of the development work. Bench checks established a baseline before control tuning, transition work and mission testing in the field.
The result and the next evidence

The delivered work included an assembled aircraft and an iterative sequence of configuration and field tests. Existing photographs show the fuselage integration, bench setup and aircraft in the field. I keep those stages visible because they explain the engineering behind the aircraft without turning a photograph into a performance claim.

title: From printed structures to a tiltrotor test platform
intro: A V-tail tricopter VTOL brought mechanical assembly and flight-control configuration into the same development loop.
sections: The challenge: connect the moving mechanisms

A tiltrotor adds a mechanical interface to the control problem. The structure, propulsion units, servos and sensors have to work as a coordinated system. My work covered printed components and assembly as well as the electronics and autopilot setup.
Use a matching test configuration

I integrated the propulsion, servos and sensors and worked with Pixhawk-family and SpeedyBee ArduPilot configurations. A matching tricopter setup helped investigate settings before wider VTOL testing. This kept configuration work tied to the actual propulsion arrangement rather than treating the aircraft as a generic multirotor.
What reached testing

The project record includes assembly, hovering and maiden-test material, alongside mission-planning and configuration work. The photographs and system overview show the development stages. They describe a working development effort, with test scope kept separate from any claim of production qualification.

title: Giving a Micro Talon vertical takeoff capability
intro: The conversion linked new lift hardware to the fixed-wing aircraft's existing cruise role.
sections: The challenge: add lift without losing the aircraft

Converting a fixed-wing airframe into a QuadPlane changes its mechanical and electrical interfaces. Four lift motors need mounting, power and control, while forward propulsion and the original flight surfaces remain part of the aircraft.
Build, configure and check the handoff

I produced mounting parts, integrated the lift propulsion and electronics, and configured the SpeedyBee F405 WING Mini with ArduPlane. Calibration, hover modes, transition parameters and mission setup were part of the same integration sequence.
The recorded result

The project includes a physical VTOL conversion and a documented flight-test sequence, including an initial QStabilize takeoff and landing. That is the validation I show. Wider transition reliability is a separate question and is not inferred from a single successful takeoff.

title: Building a 10-inch FPV aircraft for assisted flight and missions
intro: Propulsion, power, flight controls and failsafes were developed as a complete aircraft.
sections: The challenge: go beyond a frame and motors

The 6S quadcopter needed to support manual handling, assisted flight and waypoint missions. The component choices and electrical integration therefore had to serve both the aircraft's propulsion demands and its autopilot functions.
Connect hardware to behaviour

I selected propulsion and power components, integrated Pixhawk 6X and sensors, and completed wiring and calibration. I then worked on flight modes, mission setup, failsafes and PID tuning. This joined the bench integration to the behaviour that would be checked in the field.
What was tested

The documented work includes assisted-flight and mission testing, plus approximately 2 kg payload testing for this development configuration. Bench and field images show the aircraft at different stages. Those checks belong to this build and are not a payload guarantee for every 10-inch aircraft.

title: Making a compact INAV FPV build ready for flight
intro: A 3-inch platform connected power, radio control and firmware setup in a small airframe.
sections: The challenge: small aircraft still need full integration

Compact FPV aircraft leave little room for poor component placement or unclear wiring. This project brought together a 4S power system, flight-control electronics and ExpressLRS radio control within a small frame.
Bring the interfaces into one setup

I worked through the wiring, firmware configuration and control setup, including Angle and Horizon mode tuning. The objective was a coherent stabilized FPV configuration, with radio and flight-control behaviour checked together.
The delivered scope

The project record includes the build, documented wiring and flight-validation work for stabilized FPV flying. Its role is different from the autonomous mission platforms elsewhere in the portfolio. Keeping it separate makes the compact-aircraft integration work easier to see.

title: Establishing an S500 autopilot and sensor baseline
intro: A sensor-equipped quadcopter connected propulsion, navigation and telemetry before stability checks.
sections: The challenge: make the integration observable
A development aircraft needs more than a powered flight controller. GNSS, telemetry and calibrated sensors are part of understanding what the vehicle is doing and preparing useful tests.
Build the baseline

I integrated Pixhawk 6X, GNSS, telemetry and propulsion interfaces on the S500, completed calibration and parameter setup, and worked on flight-stability checks. The focus was to bring these elements into one configured development platform.
What the project shows

The delivered work is the S500 hardware integration, sensor calibration and development testing. The current image documents the avionics setup. Additional photographs can extend the build record without changing the scope of the work already described.

title: Finding where a LiDAR proximity pipeline was delayed
intro: Sensor output, autopilot input and the ground-station display needed to be examined separately.
sections: The challenge: a delayed display is not a diagnosis

The integration connected a Unitree L2 LiDAR pipeline to ArduPilot through companion computing. Proximity information appeared delayed, but the visible symptom alone could not establish whether the delay came from sensing, transport, autopilot input or display rendering.
Trace the data path

I reviewed the ROS 2 and MAVROS path into MAVLink OBSTACLE_DISTANCE, together with serial mapping and proximity settings. I separated sensor-to-autopilot latency from ground-station rendering and proposed ground checks to examine the interfaces and timing.
An actionable investigation

The output was an integration findings report with validation steps. It narrowed the questions for the next checks instead of treating an unverified tuning change as a complete solution. The public report excerpts show the approach; universal obstacle-avoidance performance is not claimed.

title: Commissioning the ground-drive stage of a hybrid aircraft
intro: The wheeled-aircraft project required its own motor-control and safety baseline.
sections: The challenge: separate the two operating modes

An aircraft that can drive on wheels brings different control paths into one platform. This engagement focused on the ground unit before the later flight-and-drive merge. It is a separate project from the drone landing on a rover.
Make ground commands explicit

I integrated the CUAV X7+ ArduRover baseline, dual VESC motor paths, skid-steer mixing and RC safety gating. The work connected the operator commands and autopilot configuration to the wheel-drive interfaces.
The delivered milestone

I documented the ground-control behaviour, setup and next integration steps in a commissioning report. The ground milestone is the completed delivery shown here. Combining wheel operation with flight was a later stage, so I do not present it as a finished hybrid-flight result.

title: Connecting perception to a usable vehicle payload
intro: Detection, camera control and video transport belong to the same integration problem.
sections: The challenge: make the output useful to the vehicle and operator

A detection model by itself is not a complete payload. The camera stream, companion computer, tracking workflow and gimbal or platform interface all have to connect. My work covered those interfaces across embedded vehicle applications.
Join compute, camera and transport

I integrated Jetson and Raspberry Pi companion computing, YOLOv8 and ByteTrack workflows, and camera or gimbal interfaces with RTSP and GStreamer video transport. On the USV work, Jetson Nano and an A8C gimbal connected first-person video and AI-detection workflows with operator visibility.
The delivered work

The contribution was integration of perception, video and platform interfaces. The project is presented as an embedded payload workflow rather than an unsupported accuracy or autonomy claim. Its supporting images provide the hardware context, with room for more application-specific material.
